source_text.ISS-0917:
id: ISS-0917
title: "Catalog SERVICE_TASK cannot execute: ServiceTaskDispatcher.catalog_lookup_stub/2 is an unconditional {:error,:not_registered}; POST /tasks/:id/complete returns 500 when the next node is a catalog-only SERVICE_TASK"
discovered_by: RELEASE-VALIDATOR
discovered_in_run: WF02-REQ432-20260930 (filed by ORCH)
discovered_at: "2026-09-30T20:50:51Z"
severity: MAJOR
owner: "ELIXIR-DEV"
description: >
  Found by WF02-REQ432-20260930 (REQ-432 live pipeline run,
  test/reports/report-20260930-WF02-REQ432-20260930.yaml; step-02b-rework1-frontend-
  dev.json). A process whose SERVICE_TASK references a service_id (catalog_entry pin) cannot
  ever execute: Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher.catalog_lookup_stub/2
  (lib/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher.ex ~411-416) returns {:error,:not_registered}
  unconditionally, so activation renders an empty URL. Measured live: completing the
  preceding human task hops synchronously into the SERVICE_TASK, the engine persists only
  EXECUTION_ERROR (affected node n3, error_type service_task_url_rendered_empty, no
  TASK_COMPLETED for the completed task) and POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/complete answers HTTP
  500 (probably needs a non-500 mapping for {:instance_execution_error,_,_} in
  lib/letflow/routers/tasks.ex). Independent of service retirement. Consequence: scenario
  platform-instance-pin-survives-catalog-change EO-001/EO-004 'the in-flight step completes
  without error' cannot be met on success; REQ-432's pipeline spec accepts the measured
  outcome (B) as a documented limitation. Needed: resolve service_id through the instance's
  PINNED service_catalog version (Letflow.Engine.PinResolver / ServiceCatalog lookup) in the
  dispatcher, then tighten the REQ-432 spec step 03 to require success. SCOPE GAP already
  noted in design docs lib/letflow/design/req373-service-catalog-version-lifecycle.md and
  lib/letflow/design/req432-rebind-pins-publish-retire-ui.md (M5). Owner ELIXIR-DEV (via
  CODE-DESIGNER). Severity MAJOR.
  NOTE (added by ORCH at close-out of the cancelled duplicate run WF02-REQ432-20260930): the
  REQ-432 implementation that actually landed on main is PR #2055 (5d7ca7bf), not this run's
  branch. Its spec (web/tests/e2e/pipelines/platform-instance-pin-survives-catalog-change
  .pipeline.e2e.spec.ts, header 'Scope note (deliberately not exercised): SERVICE_TASK dispatch')
  never drives a token onto the SERVICE_TASK node, so on main the scenario's 'the in-flight step
  completes without error' (EO-001/EO-004 step 3) is unverified; the evidence of this stub's effect
  is the duplicate run's live finding (archived on remote branch feature/WF02-REQ432-20260930,
  handoffs/WF02-REQ432-20260930/step-02b-rework1-frontend-dev.json and step-05-release-validator.json).
source_reports:
  - handoffs/WF02-REQ432-20260930/step-05-release-validator.json
  - test/reports/report-20260930-WF02-REQ432-20260930.yaml
affected_files:
  - lib/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher.ex
  - lib/letflow/routers/tasks.ex
queue_ref: Q-907  # queue allocated issue_ref ISS-0907, which collides with an existing local file; local filename kept as ISS-0917 (next free on origin/main) and GH-2057 retitled to match
github_ref: GH-2057
status: open

task.description: WF-03 Step 0.5 (registry lookup in docs/issues/*.yaml for resolved entries about SERVICE_TASK dispatch / catalog_lookup / pin resolution / instance_execution_error 500) + Step 1 (diagnose), combined. Work in the main checkout C:/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow-3 on branch feature/WF03-ISS0917-20261001 (already created and pushed; do not switch branches). DEFECT per context.source_text.ISS-0917. DO NOT trust the report's prose: reproduce (write a throwaway scratch test or run existing ones; MIX_ENV=test mix test works here, Postgres is up, see docs/anti-patterns.md for env notes). Determine and report with file:line evidence: (1) exactly how ServiceTaskDispatcher.catalog_lookup_stub/2 is called (~line 705) and what inputs (tenant_id? instance? pinned catalog version id? service_id) are available at that point; (2) the service catalog data model: lib/letflow/ service_catalog modules, Letflow.Engine.PinResolver, how an instance pins a service_catalog version / catalog_entry, what a looked-up entry must yield (url template? method? headers? auth? retry_policy?) so that the dispatcher can run it, and how the non-catalog (inline URL) SERVICE_TASK path already works so the fix can reuse it; (3) the REQ-373 / REQ-432 design docs (lib/letflow/design/req373-service-catalog-version-lifecycle.md, req432-rebind-pins-publish-retire-ui.md M5) statements about this scope gap; (4) POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/complete in lib/letflow/routers/tasks.ex: what error tuple reaches the router and the status mapping today; read lib/letflow/design/req085*.md section 5 (the row mapping {:instance_execution_error,_,_} to 500) and any decision record in docs/migration/decisions/ that bears on it, and state whether 500 is a deliberate decision or an unreviewed default, and what mapping would be right when the cause is a SERVICE_TASK execution failure (note: after a fix the happy path should succeed with 2xx; the question is whether a failing service task should still 500). NOTE open PR #2087 (fix/ISS-0942, assignee-authorization on POST /tasks/:id/complete) and PR #2089 (ISS-0918, service retry_policy) touch nearby files - run `gh pr diff 2087 --name-only` / 2089 and report overlap risk with lib/letflow/routers/tasks.ex and service_task_dispatcher.ex. (5) which existing tests cover the dispatcher/catalog and the REQ-432 pipeline spec (find under test/ and web/tests/e2e/pipelines/platform-instance-pin-survives-catalog-change.pipeline.e2e.spec.ts; also scenario platform-instance-pin-survives-catalog-change EO-001/EO-004) and what 'step 03' currently asserts. (6) tenant-data-path notes: where tenant scoping applies to catalog lookups (SECURITY-REVIEWER will gate this). Put the diagnosis in result.summary (root cause, affected files, what a fix must change, risks, whether a migration is needed, severity confirmation). Do NOT implement the fix and do NOT leave any lib/ or test/ changes behind: `git status --porcelain lib/ test/ web/` must be empty when you finish (scratch repro must be deleted). Commit nothing except your handoff file edits; ORCH commits. Complete the handoff per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 3 (status COMPLETED, result.status PASS, next_action 'Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design').

The 500 mapping decision (req085 section 5 / decision records) analysed with a recommendation

result.summary:
STEP 0.5: no resolved docs/issues entry matches (28 files mentioning SERVICE_TASK/catalog_lookup/PinResolver/instance_execution_error scanned): ISS-0930 (resolved; seeded relative URLs, inline_url path) is a different root cause; ISS-0933 (OPEN, D4: complete on ERROR instance returns 500) is the adjacent same-catch-all issue. Not a recurrence.

ROOT CAUSE (CORRECTS THE REPORT): the failure is NOT at ServiceTaskDispatcher.catalog_lookup_stub/2; the stub is never reached on this path. It fails at ACTIVATION in Letflow.Engine: lib/letflow/engine.ex:906-907 (resolve_service_task_arm_attrs/5) handles route_kind :catalog_service by calling finish_service_task_arm_attrs(config, node_id, instance_id, nil, now) with rendered_url hard-coded nil; engine.ex:911-914 validate_rendered_url(nil) -> {:error,:empty_rendered_url} -> {:empty_url_error,node_id}; the completion hop chain turns that into an EXECUTION_ERROR (engine.ex:3531, 3608-3618); no service_task_dispatches row is ever inserted. This is a deliberate REQ-215 decision (comment engine.ex:891-897; engine_test.exs:1232-1247 asserts {:activation_failed,{:service_task_url_rendered_empty,"svc"}}): the catalog resolver was simply never built. The stub: lib/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher.ex:411-416, unconditional {:error,:not_registered}; its ONLY call site is service_task_dispatcher.ex:763-766 (do_attempt_dispatch/2, poll-time, :catalog_service config_snapshot row -> handle_failure(:request_build_error)), unreachable today because activation never inserts such a row. Inputs available there: config.service_id (config_snapshot["service_id"]), row.tenant_id, tenant_schema, row.instance_id; NO pinned version id is in the snapshot (config_snapshot_map, engine.ex:931-943). Replacing only the stub would change nothing.

REPRODUCTION (throwaway test, deleted; MIX_ENV=test mix test after `mix deps.get` fetched earmark_parser): registered a global catalog entry, active definition START->HUMAN_TASK->SERVICE_TASK(service_id)->END, Engine.create ok, Engine.complete_task printed: complete_task result: {:error, {:instance_execution_error, :service_task_url_rendered_empty, {:node, "svc"}}}; event types: ["EXECUTION_ERROR","INSTANCE_STARTED"] (no TASK_COMPLETED); projection status: [["ERROR"]]; dispatch rows: [[0]]; stub: {:error,:not_registered}. Matches the report. A SERVICE_TASK directly after START fails create/2 the same way (engine.ex:596-597).

DATA MODEL: global table service_catalog (lib/letflow/service_catalog/entry.ex; PK service_id; endpoint_url, request/response_schema, required_auth NONE/API_KEY/OAUTH2/MUTUAL_TLS, timeout_ms, retry_policy (free string), scope :global|:tenant, owner_tenant_id, version, version_id uuid, status ACTIVE|RETIRED, published_at, retired_at) = the single CURRENT version; superseded versions archived by publish/3 in service_catalog_versions (version.ex; PK version_id; service_id, version, endpoint_url, required_auth, timeout_ms, retry_policy; NO scope/owner columns). Pin: ServiceCatalog.PinLookup.catalog_lookup/1 (pin_lookup.ex:57; wired in Engine.pin_lookup/2 engine.ex:1062-1064) returns %{resolved_id: version_id, version: version}; PinResolver.resolve/4 records kind :catalog_entry, ref=service_id, resolved_id=version_id in INSTANCE_STARTED payload; PinResolver.pin_for/3 (pin_resolver.ex:766, pure) and reconstruct_effective_pins/2 (pin_resolver.ex:636, includes INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND) read it back. A looked-up version yields endpoint_url (URL template), timeout_ms, retry_policy, required_auth; NO method/headers/body (those come from node attributes via ServiceTask.parse_config_from_node_attributes/1, service_task.ex ~178-215; both service_id and endpoint set -> catalog wins). No function exists that fetches a version by version_id. Inline path to reuse: engine.ex:902-904 render_service_task_url/2 ({{variables.KEY}}) -> arm attrs -> config_snapshot_map -> dispatcher :inline_url branch (service_task_dispatcher.ex:741-753: http_transport/3 behind Webhooks.UrlValidator SSRF gate, classify_failure_kind, handle_success/handle_failure). http_transport implements no required_auth handling (scope decision for designer).

WHAT A FIX MUST CHANGE (suggested shape): (a) new ServiceCatalog fn resolving a pinned version_id -> {endpoint_url, timeout_ms, retry_policy, required_auth, version}: live Entry with matching version_id (a RETIRED current row keeps its version_id), else service_catalog_versions by PK. (b) Resolve at ACTIVATION: pass the instance's effective pins into prepare_service_task_dispatch/5 (engine.ex:851) / resolve_service_task_arm_attrs; for :catalog_service use PinResolver.pin_for(pins,:catalog_entry,service_id), fetch the pinned version, render its endpoint_url with render_service_task_url/2, and store the resolved URL (+ version_id/version for audit) in config_snapshot so the dispatcher's existing inline machinery runs it; convert the dispatcher's :catalog_service branch from stub to snapshot-driven and retire catalog_lookup_stub/2 with its tests (service_task_dispatcher_test.exs:201-290) and doc claims (moduledoc, design service_task_dispatcher.md 5.3, INV-STD-8). Pin sources per call site: create/2 has `pins` in scope (engine.ex ~520-570); other callers (completion hop chain engine.ex:3500 via prepare_service_task_dispatch_for_completion/7; timer sites engine.ex:2463, 2684, 3088 via prepare_service_task_dispatch_abort_on_empty_url) must use PinResolver.reconstruct_effective_pins(instance_id, prefix: prefix). Missing pin for a service_id -> typed error; MUST NOT fall back to the live current row (would defeat the REQ-373/432 pin guarantee). No migration needed (all columns exist; config_snapshot is jsonb, extra keys backward compatible).

DESIGN DOC STATEMENTS: req373 design (lib/letflow/design/req373-service-catalog-version-lifecycle.md) covers pin resolution/retire only and leaves dispatch out (scope gap ~lines 32-45, 92, 233); req432-rebind-pins-publish-retire-ui.md M5 restates dispatcher gap as out of scope; service_task_dispatcher.md 5.3/INV-STD-8 and service_task.md line 96 defer the real lookup to 'S6'. engine_test.exs:1232 and engine_pin_resolver_catalog_test.exs:127 document the activation failure as expected and sidestep it.

500 MAPPING: Router: Letflow.Routers.Tasks.handle_complete/3 (tasks.ex ~314) -> Engine.complete_task -> interpret_complete_result (engine.ex ~4540-4549) turns the committed {:execution_error,args} outcome into {:error,{:instance_execution_error,error_type,affected}} AFTER the Multi commits (ERROR state persisted by design, req061 5.4); handle_complete_result/2 has 400/422/404/409(task_not_pending)/422(changeset) clauses and a catch-all `{:error,_}` -> Response.internal_error (tasks.ex ~357-375, whose comment lists {:instance_execution_error,_,_}). Source: lib/letflow/design/req085-task-routes-write.md 5.5.1 row 'every other member of complete_error()' -> 500, justified as 'structurally unreachable ... or genuine data-integrity/downstream failure this caller cannot fix by retrying', by analogy with REQ-083 3.5. No decision record in docs/migration/decisions mentions it and docs/anti-patterns.md has no entry. Verdict: a deliberate-by-analogy but never individually reviewed default for the execution-error case, and its rationale fits poorly: the request durably recorded state, the instance is now ERROR (operator-visible), and the same path also covers no_matching_gateway_edge, so ordinary data-driven process errors surface as 5xx. Caller retry is pointless (task not completed). RECOMMENDATION: add a dedicated clause before the catch-all mapping {:instance_execution_error, error_type, affected} to a 409-style 4xx (Response.conflict, detail naming only the error_type atom, no variables/affected internals), consistent with ISS-0933 (open; ERROR instance -> 4xx); keep 500 for real integrity errors; record via REQ-085 5.5.1 amendment or a decision record (REVIEWER-visible, it changes a documented table); coordinate with ISS-0933. After the dispatch fix the happy path returns 200 (instance_status :active, current_nodes [svc] since SERVICE_TASK dispatch is asynchronous via the poller), so 'completes without error' (EO-001/EO-004) is observable via the HTTP 200 plus a dispatch row reaching 'advanced'/history. A failing service task at dispatch time never touches this endpoint (poller handles it); only activation-time errors (empty/unresolvable URL, missing pin) reach the 4xx mapping.

OPEN PR OVERLAP: PR #2087 (ISS-0942) touches lib/letflow/routers/tasks.ex (handle_complete/3 rewritten with Tasks.authorize_completion/3 and three new 403 handle_complete_result clauses inserted immediately before the catch-all: exactly where our new clause belongs; HIGH textual conflict risk, trivially resolvable; land after #2087 or rebase) and lib/letflow/engine.ex (doc-comment hunks only near ~120-135 and ~1931; low risk), plus lib/letflow/tasks.ex, req048/req085 docs. PR #2089 (ISS-0918) touches instances.ex, routers/instances.ex, routers/admin_services.ex (adds max_retries/retry_policy to service_record_json) and tests: NO file overlap with tasks.ex or service_task_dispatcher.ex, but semantic overlap on retry_policy surfacing; the fix should not interpret retry_policy until #2089's shape is known. Neither PR touches service_task_dispatcher.ex, service_catalog*.ex, or engine.ex activation code.

TESTS: unit: test/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher_test.exs (stub 201-212; :catalog_service routing 216-300), service_task_test.exs, engine_test.exs:1220-1250 (expects the activation failure; must be flipped), engine_pin_resolver_catalog_test.exs (REQ-373 AC2-5; its graph_human_task_then_service_task fixture is a ready basis for a fail-first test), service_catalog_test.exs, routers/admin_services_publish_retire_test.exs, routers/tasks_test.exs. E2E: web/tests/e2e/pipelines/platform-instance-pin-survives-catalog-change.pipeline.e2e.spec.ts has 'Scope note (deliberately not exercised): SERVICE_TASK dispatch' (lines 49-61) and never completes the HUMAN_TASK. Its pl.step('03...') (line 243) is retire v1 then publish v2 via the admin GUI/API and asserts version '2' and status ACTIVE; step 04 (line 296) asserts the pins panel still shows v1. The scenario test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/platform/instance-pin-survives-catalog-change.yaml step 3 / EO-001 / EO-004 ('completes the step that uses the retired version without error') is the UNVERIFIED part; so 'tighten step 03' really means adding a new step after 03/04 that completes the HUMAN_TASK and asserts HTTP 200 plus a dispatch advance using the v1 endpoint (not v2). Seeded endpoints are https://example.test/... (not resolvable): a real e2e needs a controllable mock URL (see ISS-0930 SERVICE_TASK_MOCK_BASE_URL precedent; the SSRF gate blocks localhost).

TENANT SCOPING (for SECURITY-REVIEWER): service_catalog and service_catalog_versions are GLOBAL tables (public schema, no tenant prefix; entry.ex moduledoc; deviation from decision 0003 B); visibility is app-level scope/owner_tenant_id (ServiceCatalog.get_for_tenant/2, list_for_tenant/2, ServiceScopeValidator via scope_validator_lookup at definition activation). PinLookup.catalog_lookup/1 (pin_lookup.ex:57) does Repo.get(Entry, service_id) with NO tenant argument or visibility check, and the archive table has no scope/owner columns, so a new by-version resolver must (1) take tenant_id and apply the get_for_tenant three-way rule by checking the live Entry by service_id for scope/owner (invisible == not found, no disclosure), (2) take version_id only from the instance's own event-sourced pins in the tenant schema, never from caller input, (3) keep UrlValidator.validate before :httpc (endpoint_url is tenant-authored for scope :tenant), (4) not log or echo variables/headers. Dispatcher reads/writes already use the tenant_schema prefix; keep. Separate pre-existing observation worth its own issue: PinLookup.catalog_lookup/1 is not tenant-scoped (activation-time ServiceScopeValidator is the only guard).

SEVERITY: MAJOR confirmed (catalog-pinned SERVICE_TASKs cannot execute at all; instance goes ERROR; REQ-373/432 pin guarantee unverifiable end to end). Not BLOCKER: inline-URL service tasks (all QA seeds after ISS-0930) work. Chain: CODE-DESIGNER -> ELIXIR-DEV; SECURITY-REVIEWER gate mandatory (tenant data path). Housekeeping: no lib/test/web changes left (git status --porcelain lib test web empty; scratch test deleted); `mix deps.get` only fetched earmark_parser into untracked deps/, mix.lock unchanged.

issues.description: Catalog-pinned SERVICE_TASK never executes: Engine.resolve_service_task_arm_attrs (engine.ex:906) passes rendered_url nil for :catalog_service so activation aborts with service_task_url_rendered_empty; catalog_lookup_stub/2 is unreachable. Fix = resolve the instance's PINNED service_catalog version at activation.

POST /tasks/:id/complete maps {:instance_execution_error,_,_} to 500 via REQ-085 5.5.1 catch-all (unreviewed default); recommend dedicated 409-style clause, coordinate with ISS-0933 and PR #2087 (same region of tasks.ex).
PinLookup.catalog_lookup/1 and the version archive are not tenant-scoped (global tables); a new by-version resolver must apply get_for_tenant visibility. Consider a separate issue for PinLookup.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design
